reason: 'Multicéphale' means bearing many heads. That is a count of capitula in the inflorescence, not a quality of its own.
'Non tordu' = not twisted. It negates PATO_0002445 torsioned, whose EXACT synonym is twisted.

label: curvinerved
definition: A branched quality inhering in a leaf venation by virtue of its primary veins arising at or near the base and running in curved arcs towards the apex, where they converge. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991202 triplinerved and FLOPO:0991201 pinnately veined; PATO has only PATO:0001968 parallelodromous, whose veins do not arc.
reason: This is a standard venation type with no PATO or FLOPO term. Parallel-veined goes to parallelodromous, but curved, converging primaries are a different type.
It refers to an inflorescence type defined by one genus in one flora's treatment. It means nothing outside that context.
'Bicostate or unicostate' (moss leaves) counts the costae. It is the same kind of word as '5-nerved'.
'Sub-' + velutinous means approximately velvety, as with 'suborbicular'. PATO_0104041 velutinous exists.
It is used almost only for lichen apothecium walls, which are fungal structures outside PO. A term for so few bearers would be doubtful.

target: new: colour tinge (reddish purple PATO_0104079 as a tinge)
reason: A tint is a weak overlay of a colour on the ground colour, here limited to part of the stem. It is better as a tinge pattern over the existing colour classes than as one class per tinted colour.
Short shoots and axes covered with leaf or flower scars are scarred: PATO_0001850.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values: ovate PATO_0001891 / spherical PATO_0001499)
reason: It joins two values into a shape between ovoid and globose. That is a continuum of two existing terms, not a new shape.
Allium bulb coats are described as fibrous or not. 'Without fibers' negates FLOPO:0991026 fibrous; these fibres are not PO fiber cells.

label: mammiform
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a nipple: a rounded protuberance ending in a small blunt point. NOTE: PATO:0002108 papillary is a tumour growth pattern, not this shape.
reason: It is a genuine stigma shape and no PATO or FLOPO shape covers it.
A stem branched like a panicle has a panicle-like architecture. FLOPO:0991198 already lists branch among its bearers. '2 ×' is a count of branching orders and goes to the count pattern.
Oviform = egg-shaped. PATO_0001891 ovate has egg-shaped and ovoid as synonyms; for bulbs and fruits it is the 3-D reading.
'Thyrses panicle-shaped' means the architecture resembles a panicle: FLOPO:0991198.

label: homosporous
definition: A morphology quality inhering in a plant or sporangium by virtue of its producing spores of one kind only, not differentiated into microspores and megaspores. NOTE: Botany-specific, like FLOPO:0991137 heterostylous; its opposite, heterosporous, may be added later.
reason: It is a basic character of ferns and lycophytes with no PATO term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values: olive colour PATO_0104336 becoming black PATO_0000317)
reason: Nigrescent means turning black. The word joins an olive colour with a blackening, which is a change between two existing colours.

target: new: quality of a named part (awn PO_0025349 present + scabrous FLOPO:0991058 on the awn)
reason: It joins a part (an awn is present) with a quality of that part (the awn is scabrous). Both terms exist.
Allium bulb coats marked with a network formed by the cell outlines are reticulate. FLOPO:0991100 covers a surface marked by a network.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023 filiform PATO_0104351)
reason: It is a scale whose tip is drawn out into a thread. That is a shape (filiform) of the apex region, not a new quality.
'Sub-' + square means approximately square. PATO_0000413 exists.

label: flagelliflorous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its bearing its flowers or inflorescences on long, slender, whip-like leafless branches that arise from the base of the trunk and often lie on or in the ground. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991175 cauliflorous.
reason: It is a distinct botanical habit (e.g. Ficus) and a sibling of cauliflorous, which was already added.

target: new: colour tinge (brown PATO_0000952 as a tinge)
reason: A brown tinge on sheaths and stem bases is a tinge over the ground colour. Handle it with the tinge pattern, not a term per colour.

target: new: colour tinge (light brown PATO_0001246 as a tinge)
reason: Same case as the other '-tinged' words: a light brown tinge, using PATO_0001246.
'Sub-' + corymbose means approximately corymb-like. PATO_0002455 exists.

label: tetracytic
definition: A morphology quality inhering in a stomatal complex by virtue of its guard cells being surrounded by four subsidiary cells, two lateral and two polar. NOTE: A count of subsidiary cells (PO_0000284) would lose their arrangement; other stomatal types (anomocytic, paracytic) are siblings to add when met.
reason: Stomatal type is a standard anatomical character and PATO has no stomatal-type terms.
In FNA sedges, 'flagged' leaves have a blade, while 'bladeless' leaves are sheaths only. So the word states that a leaf blade is present.
Bulbiferous inflorescences bear bulbils. In PO, bulbil is a synonym of aerial tuber, so 'not bulbiferous' states its absence.
'Scales unsegmented or 2-segmented' means not divided into segments. It negates PATO_0002312 segmented.
Bulblet is a synonym of bulb in PO, so the phrase states that bulblets are absent at the nodes. (The 'ray' bearer here is an umbel ray, not a ray flower.)
